items.summary: A new report from the Schneider Electric Research Institute (SERI), released at UN COP31, models how solar paired with battery storage could reduce Europe's electricity system costs by up to 40 per cent in the 2030s. The study ran 40,500 scenarios across combinations of solar, battery and grid costs. SERI quotes Laurent Bataille: 'Solar is the fuel, the battery is the power plant.' Savings could add roughly 0.8 per cent to global GDP by 2030.
items.title: Solar and Battery Harmony Could Cut European Electricity Costs by Up to 40%

items.summary: EU leaders gathered informally in Dublin on Friday for their first artificial intelligence discussion, but the agenda was overshadowed by a dispute over who should represent Europe in Ukraine peace talks. European Council President António Costa added the issue after Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni warned that multiple EU formats made negotiations less credible. Costa put himself forward as natural representative; Luxembourg's Luc Frieden supported him, while foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas argued for her and Costa to lead on security. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy urged a decision by month's end. Germany defended the E3 format with France, UK, Poland and Italy. The summit also featured Mistral AI's Arthur Mensch and Nobel laureate Geoffrey Hinton addressing Europe's AI competitiveness and existential risks.
items.title: Ukraine Envoy Row Hijacks EU Leaders' First AI Summit

items.summary: Poland's East Shield initiative aims to fortify its eastern border, but conservationists propose 'warwilding'—restoring forests as natural barriers. Scientists like Michal Zmihorski argue tanks cannot traverse dense woodlands, gaining military support from Marek Pietrzak. NGOs including PTOP rewild waterways amid drainage damage over 700 kilometers and road-widening threats across 2,000 kilometers.
items.title: Białowieża Forest Defense and Rewilding Efforts in Poland

items.summary: The FBI says state-sponsored hackers from North Korea stole over $400 million in cryptocurrency through a scheme called FaceStealer, which used fake video calls to steal identities. More than 900 victims were targeted in the last 18 months. The bureau links these thefts to Pyongyang's weapons funding and notes similar attacks on Binance.
items.title: FBI: North Korean Hackers Used Fake Video Calls in $400m Crypto Heist

items.summary: The Election Commission released draft electoral rolls showing voter increases of up to 3% across nine states and Union Territories following the special intensive revision. Goa led at 3%, followed by Rajasthan's 2.2%. Other regions recorded smaller gains, including Kerala (1.5%), Bihar and Tamil Nadu (1.8%). Draft figures for some areas remain below pre-revision counts. The exercise has drawn concerns over potential voter exclusion and political misuse.
items.title: Voter Rolls Rise in Nine States and UTs After Special Intensive Revision

items.summary: A military vehicle carrying Army personnel overturned during a training exercise and crashed into a tree, injuring seven people. The accident occurred while the group traveled from Golconda Army Camp in Hyderabad to Shabad town in Rangareddy district, Telangana. Two of the injured are reportedly in critical condition. They were taken to the Army Hospital in Golconda for treatment.
items.title: Army Vehicle Accident in Telangana Leaves Seven Personnel Injured

items.summary: PM Modi attended Bengaluru's Prasanthi Kutiram Golden Jubilee, highlighting global expansion of Ayurveda and yoga. Over 150 Ayurveda courses worldwide are recognised through agreements with 28 countries. Yogasana is now part of major sports events via the Ministry of AYUSH. Initiatives like the e-Ayush visa support cross-border patient travel. The address also emphasised preventive health integration following reports of significant poverty reduction.
items.title: Ayurveda and Yoga Expand Globally Under Modi's Recognition Push

items.summary: The briefing opens with President Donald Trump saying he may use military force against Iran "right now" if US allies and ships are threatened, while Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy described a planned Russia-Ukraine prisoner exchange as the largest of its kind. Israeli strikes killed 11 Palestinians in Gaza on Thursday, wounding around 40 others across Jabalia al-Nazla, near Al-Shifa Hospital, Deir al-Balah and Khan Younis. Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan urged sustained effort to keep the Paris Agreement's 1.5-degree target within reach at COP31.
items.title: Morning Briefing: Nov. 13

items.summary: On Friday (13 November 2026), South Korean President Lee Jae Myung reaffirmed his administration's commitment to capital market reforms, addressing domestic stock undervaluation he called an "unreasonable abnormality". Speaking at the Korea Exchange amid KOSPI volatility in the mid-5,000-point range—down from a late-June record of 9,114.55—he cited geopolitical tensions and urged restoring investor confidence through institutional reforms and intensified enforcement against unfair trading practices.
items.title: South Korean President Vows Capital Market Reforms and Crackdown on Stock Manipulation

items.summary: Luke J. Lindberg, the new WFP executive director, called for an end to fighting in Sudan during a visit to Goz Al-Salam Camp, where hundreds of thousands face famine. The WFP fed 4 million people in August but cut aid due to funding shortfalls, leaving 900,000 without help; it now seeks $520 million to feed 5.4 million through April 2027. Sudan's war since April 2023 has created the world's largest humanitarian crisis, affecting about 34 million people.
items.title: UN World Food Programme Chief Urges End to Sudan War Amid Deepening Famine Crisis

items.summary: Activist Sonam Wangchuk claimed Thursday he was placed under house arrest by police ahead of Ladakh's council polls, alleging the move curtails his right to protest. He challenged a Section 163 order valid for 60 days and alleged social media suppression. Panchayat elections are set for November 21; eight Autonomous Hill Development Councils vote December 4. Civil society groups and MP Mohmad Haneefa have urged postponement amid harsh winter conditions.
items.title: Ladakh Activist Sonam Wangchuk Claims House Arrest Ahead of Council Polls

items.summary: Capital-market stocks in India are gaining momentum as equities rebounded from late October, driven by lower crude oil prices and funds rotating out of a faltering global AI trade. Analysts at Sky Links Capital Group and BofA Global Research see structural growth potential ahead.
items.title: India Equity Surge Brightens Outlook for Exchanges and Brokerages

items.summary: The Tamil Nadu Fisheries Department banned fishing across coastal villages from Vembar to Periyathazhai after a low-pressure area over the Bay of Bengal is expected to intensify into a cyclone. Over 270 mechanised, 2,000 country and 5,000 fibre boats remain moored, affecting more than 50,000 fishermen in Tuticorin district. The India Meteorological Department warns squally winds may hit the Gulf of Mannar and Comorin on November 13-14.
items.title: Cyclone Threat Halts Fishing in Thoothukudi and Tuticorin

items.summary: At Arlington National Cemetery during a Veterans Day wreath-laying ceremony, a sentinel reprimanded a group including US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth. The incident prompted the Pentagon to award Specialist Thomas Iglesias a Joint Service Commendation Medal for his duties at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier. BBC's Bernd Debusmann explains why Hegseth's party was disciplined and the history behind strict rules governing visitor behaviour, emphasising the importance of maintaining silence at the tomb.
items.title: Military cemetery decorum behind Hegseth's Veterans Day reprimand

items.summary: Crude oil prices were on course for a second weekly loss after two days of gains amid mixed signals from the Middle East. Brent traded at $95.87 and WTI at $88.49 per barrel, well below mid-October peaks but above pre-war February levels. Iranian attacks on Hormuz tankers continued, with reports that four vessels were targeted for noncompliance. Saudi Arabia said crude production rebounded to 10.56 million barrels daily last month.
items.title: Oil Prices Head for Second Weekly Loss Despite Middle East Attacks

items.summary: A global Microsoft outage disrupted e-mail communications for Singapore banks, the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS), and other institutions on November 13. Affected banks including DBS, UOB, OCBC, HSBC, and Maybank offered customers alternative contact methods such as hotlines, relationship managers, websites, ATMs, cards, digibank, and PayLah!, which remained operational. MAS monitored the situation while advising vigilance against phishing scams exploiting the disruption.
items.title: Singapore Banks and MAS Navigate Microsoft Outage with Alternative Channels

items.summary: Microsoft suffered a worldwide Outlook outage Thursday, Nov. 12, 2026, attributed to elevated infrastructure load rather than hacking. The disruption spread globally within an hour across 74 countries and affected products including Teams and Copilot. Executive Charles Lamanna apologized; Microsoft paused deployments and restarted servers amid limited recovery.
items.title: Global Microsoft Outlook Outage on November 12, 2026

items.summary: In mid-May, short seller Culper Research raised concerns about Nvidia Corp.'s exposure to China. Six months later, founder Christian Lamarco drew renewed attention to the 40-page report he published on the semiconductor giant. Citing Bloomberg and The New York Times investigations alongside its own research, it questioned the relationship between then-CEO Jensen Huang and Alice Huang of Megaspeed International, describing them as 'uncomfortably close' and calling her a suspected Chinese spy—allegations that remain unverified.
items.title: Nvidia's China Concerns: What Culper Research Flagged in Its May Report

items.summary: A global Microsoft outage affected GP surgeries, police forces, pharmacies and MPs across the UK. Services urged patients to phone rather than use online forms or messaging platforms like Teams. The London Ambulance Service, major airports including Heathrow, Manchester and Stansted, and intelligence operations remained unaffected as they avoid Microsoft tools. Microsoft blamed higher-than-usual server stress for the disruption.
items.title: Microsoft Outage Disrupts UK GPs, Police and Pharmacies

items.summary: Businessline, citing Vested Finance—a platform for Indians to invest in US stocks—reports that Nvidia share trading activity from India surged nearly 400% on November 5th amid a broader semiconductor sell-off. Over the prior 10 sessions, Nvidia accounted for ~70% of combined volume; buying rose further to ~80% during November 9–10 as shares fell 9.51%, wiping out roughly $430 billion in market value.
items.title: Global investing platform Vested reports nearly 400% jump in trading activity of Nvidia shares from India

items.summary: A Reuters review of more than 150 Chinese procurement notices, investment plans, construction contracts and corporate disclosures identified computing projects built around restricted Nvidia processors with a combined reported value exceeding $3.2 billion (23 billion yuan). The findings show continued demand for Nvidia hardware despite US export controls that the company says have effectively shut it out of China's data-centre market.
items.title: $3 billion in China AI projects tied to Nvidia

items.summary: A global Microsoft outage entered its second day, disrupting workplace services including Outlook and Teams for users in India and elsewhere. As of an update at 11:16 am on Friday, the service health page showed degradation across Microsoft 365 business and enterprise customers as well as consumer products. The company reported pursuing multiple workstreams to identify a traffic influx cause while recovering backend servers, stating it was not aware of any malicious activity behind the incident.
items.title: Microsoft Outage Enters Second Day Amid Reports of No Malicious Activity

items.summary: Microsoft reported on Friday that it was still struggling to recover from a global outage affecting its services, which had persisted for more than 12 hours. Charles Lamanna ruled out a cyberattack as the cause and noted positive results for service stability and increased capacity following traffic optimization actions being rolled out across affected regions. Downdetector complaints peaked shortly after 7 pm Thursday in Spain, with problems reported in more than 70 countries; a second wave began around 7 am Friday morning and was twice as large in volume. The outage disrupted Outlook, Teams (over 320 million users), SharePoint Online, Copilot, OneDrive and OneNote. Microsoft's affected services include over 450 million corporate users and 95 million individual customers. Australia invoked a digital resilience agreement with the company, while Japan reported problems largely related to communications.
items.title: Microsoft Fails to Restore Services After More Than 12 Hours of Global Disruption

items.summary: US lawmakers summoned Nvidia co-founder and ex-CEO Jensen Huang in December after he resigned amid extramarital affairs, including one with Alice Huang, a suspected Chinese intelligence asset. The scandal erased nearly half a trillion dollars from Nvidia's market value (quantity-2253-2265) while raising national-security fears about sensitive US technology. Senator Tim Scott requested testimony before the Senate Banking Committee; three House committees threatened subpoenas for a closed-door interview. Beijing rejected espionage allegations, and Singapore barred Alice Huang in February over inaccurate information to investigators.
items.title: Lawmakers Summon Nvidia's Jensen Huang Over Suspected Spy Affair

items.summary: NVIDIA's Board of Directors announced Thursday that Jensen Huang has resigned as president, chief executive officer and board member, effective immediately. CFO Colette Kress was appointed interim CEO while continuing her role as executive vice president and CFO. The board will consider internal and external candidates for a permanent successor.
items.title: Jensen Huang Resigns as NVIDIA CEO; Colette Kress Named Interim Chief Executive

items.summary: European and Asian equities fell Friday after Jensen Huang stepped down abruptly as Nvidia CEO amid national-security concerns, prompting investors to weigh the impact on the global AI industry. Colette Kress became interim chief while oil prices rose following Trump's rejection of a deal with Iran.
items.title: European shares fall as Nvidia CEO’s exit raises doubts over AI boom

items.summary: A Microsoft outage disrupted Outlook, Teams, and Copilot worldwide, affecting aviation and financial sectors in India. Air India rerouted email traffic while keeping flights normal; IndiGo advised passengers to use 6E Skai for support.
items.title: Microsoft Outage Disrupts Air India and IndiGo Services Globally

items.summary: "The last few weeks have been turbulent for Nvidia, the world's largest semiconductor company by market capitalisation," as CEO Jensen Huang stepped down amid reports linking his alleged affair partner Alice Huang to Chinese intelligence. US officials suspect her links but say they remain unestablished; Beijing rejects them and calls them a pretext for restricting China's technology development. The departure arrives just days before Trump meets Xi Jinping at the APEC summit in Shenzhen on 18-19 November, raising questions about whether the scandal complicates an already tense US-China relationship over semiconductor exports and AI chips. Analysts say it is unlikely to immediately change Washington's approach but may intensify domestic pressure for stricter export controls."
items.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang Steps Down Amid Spy Allegations Ahead of Trump-Xi APEC Meeting

items.summary: A global Microsoft outage spanning November 12-13 disrupted cloud services far beyond workplace emails, affecting airline operations in India—SpiceJet cancelled three flights from Delhi while IndiGo's email support faltered—and government departments across Japan, Australia, and the US. The recovery proved difficult as servers became unresponsive under renewed traffic.
items.title: Microsoft Outage Impact on Airlines and Government Operations

items.summary: At COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye on 13 November 2026, Brazil's environment minister Joao Paulo Ribeiro Capobianco said the government under President Lula focuses on restoring environmental protections rather than confronting former President Jair Bolsonaro. Ministerial quotes emphasize moving past Bolsonaro and protecting the forest. Deforestation in the Amazon fell about 71% since Lula returned to office in January 2023, while reducing losses elsewhere could prevent roughly 560 million tons of greenhouse gas emissions. Brazil is advancing roadmaps on deforestation prevention and fossil fuels, promoting the Tropical Forests Forever Facility and calling for $1.3 trillion in climate finance; 44 countries have not yet submitted updated NDCs.
items.title: Brazil's Environment Minister Prioritizes Amazon Reforestation Over Confrontation With Bolsonaro at COP31

items.summary: A coalition led by the Alliance for Secure AI filed a lawsuit in San Francisco Superior Court against Anthropic, Google, Meta, OpenAI and SpaceX Super Intelligence (SpaceXSI), seeking to halt advanced AI development on safety grounds. Brendan Steinhauser accused executives of advancing powerful systems they cannot reliably control or stop from harm.
items.title: Coalition Sues Five AI Companies Over Loss of Control

items.summary: Nvidia's co-founder Jensen Huang resigned Thursday after admitting two extramarital affairs, one with Alice Huang—a former Megaspeed executive whom US intelligence reportedly flagged as a Chinese spy. The scandal erased roughly $450 billion from Nvidia's value and raised national-security concerns amid the US-China chip race. CFO Colette Kress will lead as interim CEO while the board searches for a successor; Trump suggested Tim Cook, though lawmakers demanded answers ahead of his China summit.
items.title: Jensen Huang Resigns as Nvidia CEO Amid China-Spy Scandal

items.summary: Microsoft's outage began Thursday and continued Friday into its second day without full restoration; the company found no evidence of malicious activity. It disrupted banking in Hong Kong (Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs), government services and schools in Australia under Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke—who compared it to CrowdStrike's July 2024 incident—and Japan, where officials resorted to physical documents. Philippine courts reported delays; Singapore, IndiGo and Akasa Air also affected. Downdetector logged disruptions across 74 countries within an hour.
items.title: Global Microsoft Outage Disrupts Banking, Government and Airlines Across Multiple Countries

items.summary: Microsoft confirmed that this month's Patch Tuesday updates cause Windows activation and licensing failures with error code 0x80041008, Invalid parameter (SWbemObjectEx). Organizations automating activation via the Software Licensing Management Tool or running slmgr.vbs commands on affected clients—Windows 10 21H2/22H2 and Windows 11 23H2—and servers face errors during KMS configuration. Devices activated for up to 180 days remain active, while those with the client key installed but not using SLMGR are unaffected.
items.title: Microsoft Confirms Windows Activation Failures After November Updates

items.summary: A global Microsoft service disruption, described as the tech giant's most severe in recent memory, has affected communication channels across several Indian airlines. IndiGo and Akasa Air reported delays or loss of email support services amid the outage; both advised passengers to use alternative channels—IndiGo via its 6E Skai AI-powered service, and Akasa through its 24/7 Akasa Care Centre at +91 9606 112131. Air India said its flight operations remained unaffected while temporarily rerouting emails to maintain support within its usual 24-hour timeline. The outage persisted for over 15 hours as of Friday afternoon, with Microsoft attributing the failure to a core process on affected servers becoming overwhelmed.
items.title: Microsoft Outage Disrupts Indian Airlines' Email Support Channels

items.summary: After weeks denying infidelity allegations and fighting to keep his job, Jensen Huang surrendered unconditionally late Wednesday night. Witnesses described him looking broken, his legendary energy depleted, having abandoned his usual take-charge demeanor for phrases like “whatever” and “I don’t care.” In the room, observers concluded he had simply given up — a stark contrast to the meticulous leader who built Nvidia into a multitrillion-dollar AI chip powerhouse.
items.title: ‘I’m a piece of s---’: Jensen Huang’s last hours as Nvidia CEO

items.summary: Taiwan was shocked when FBI probes into Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's alleged affair with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, a suspected Beijing spy, tarnished his rock-star image. Huang resigned Thursday amid calls to step down after also facing allegations of an extramarital affair with an employee. He apologized in an open letter.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's China Spy Scandal Shakes Taiwan

items.summary: Jensen Huang resigned immediately from Nvidia amid reports of multiple extramarital affairs, including one involving a woman suspected by US intelligence of being a Chinese spy. Colette Kress leads as interim CEO while the board weighs internal and external candidates. Sanjay Mehrotra (Micron), Nikesh Arora (Palo Alto Networks) and Thomas Kurian (Google Cloud) are among potential successors.
items.title: Three Indian-origin CEOs in race to replace Jensen Huang as Nvidia chief

items.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang stepped down Thursday amid reports of extramarital affairs, including with a suspected Chinese spy. As the public face of Nvidia—the most valuable company on Wall Street alongside Apple—his departure sends ripples through an industry where competitors like Broadcom, Intel and AMD saw shares rise as customers consider diversifying suppliers. Analysts suggest this could transform what was effectively a monopoly into competitive 'horse race,' potentially strengthening AI supply chains long-term. Huang's role extended beyond technology; he was a political advocate with access to Washington and Beijing whose resignation introduces uncertainty well beyond Nvidia itself, especially amid questions about massive AI spending.
items.title: Nvidia Scandal Fallout May Dampen AI Boom Exuberance

items.summary: A global Microsoft outage disrupted airline operations across India on Friday, beginning Thursday when the outage affected Outlook and Teams. SpiceJet reported three flight cancellations from Delhi to Pune, Leh and Mumbai, plus two delays to flights heading to Darbhanga and Mumbai. Air India said its operations remained normal while it rerouted email traffic but continued responding within 24 hours. The disruption raised concerns for businesses relying on Microsoft's platforms.
items.title: Global Microsoft Outage Disrupts Airline Services in India

items.summary: Singapore barred former Megaspeed chief executive Alice Huang from re-entering the country after police found she downplayed her role during investigations. The Ministry of Home Affairs said she received a stern warning and left in February, though it stressed she was not investigated for espionage. Singapore's probe into Megaspeed continues independently.
items.title: Singapore Bars Nvidia Scandal Figure Alice Huang After Downplaying Her Megaspeed Role

items.summary: Nvidia's longtime CFO Colette Kress has been tapped to lead the company on an interim basis after co-founder Jensen Huang stepped down amid scandal. As a pragmatic counterweight who repeatedly pushed back against Huang's risky AI financing deals, Kress is seen as able to stabilize markets during the leadership transition. However, many investors question whether she can preserve the technological risk-taking that made Nvidia dominant. Shares slumped 14 per cent on Thursday before closing down 4.3 per cent.
items.title: Colette Kress Named Interim CEO of Nvidia as Jensen Huang Steps Down Amid Scandal

items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India granted in-principle approval on November 12, 2026 to appoint Pratap Singh as Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Fino Payments Bank for a three-year term. The appointment follows the departure of former CEO Rishi Gupta and remains subject to shareholder consent. It coincides with the bank's proposed conversion into a small finance bank.
items.title: RBI Approves New CEO for Fino Payments Bank Amid Small Finance Conversion Plans

items.summary: Bloomberg News reported on Thursday (Nov 12) that Samsung is in talks to acquire Modine Manufacturing, a US-listed maker of data center cooling systems. The deal could close within weeks but no final decision has been made and another suitor may emerge. Shares surged 29% after the report; Modine's market value was about $5.6 billion as of Thursday (LSEG). Reuters could not verify it.
items.title: Samsung in talks to buy Modine

items.summary: US buyout firm Advent International has put Singapore tutor chain The Learning Lab up for sale a second time since 2021, aiming to raise about US$400 million to $500 million (S$514.6 million to S$643.3 million) partly to repay a S$265 million private credit facility maturing in 2027.
items.title: Advent International Re-Lists Singapore Tutor Chain The Learning Lab for Sale

items.summary: WTO Director-General Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala thanked Ireland for renewed support of the STDF. Minister Neale Richmond said Ireland is proud to back the facility that helps developing countries participate in global trade. The EUR 200,000 contribution supports the STDF Strategy 2025-2030 and sanitary and phytosanitary capacity development. Since its creation, the STDF has funded more than 275 projects benefiting developing economies.
items.title: Ireland Contributes EUR 200,000 to WTO Standards and Trade Development Facility

items.summary: After Nvidia announced CEO Jensen Huang's resignation on Thursday, its stock fell roughly $546 billion at market open. The scandal—centered on reported affairs with an employee and a former executive tied to China's Ministry of State Security—has since erased more than $1 trillion in valuation from the company worth about $5.2 trillion before it began.
items.title: Nvidia's Stock Plunge After Jensen Huang Resignation Over Alleged Affairs

items.summary: Bharti Airtel founder and chairman Sunil Bharti Mittal urged Indian mobile tariffs to rise to around ₹350 per month per user, citing rising operating costs—oil, electricity, staff and administrative—and the need for major telecom infrastructure investment. He noted current rates were too low, having previously set ₹300 as appropriate a decade ago amid inflation. Mittal highlighted India's tower gap versus China (about 3,50,000 towers), calling for at least doubling capacity, while noting 5G investments had underperformed revenue expectations. He argued ₹350 would still leave India among the world's cheapest markets and remain affordable.
items.title: Airtel's Sunil Mittal Calls for ₹350 Monthly Mobile Tariffs in India

items.summary: Nvidia's board removed CEO Jensen Huang effective immediately after reports of extramarital affairs with employees, compounded by his admitted relationship with Alice Huang, whom US intelligence suspects spies for China. CFO Colette Kress became interim CEO while the board sought a permanent successor among executives or family members. Market capitalization fell over $600 billion to $4.2 trillion, and shares dropped more than 9% premarket Thursday. Analysts cite key-person risk from Huang's three-decade leadership but expect limited near-term sales impact given entrenched AI demand.
items.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang Resignation Amid Spy and Affair Revelations

items.summary: Lok Sabha opposition leader Rahul Gandhi accused the Modi government on Friday of tapping his phone, claiming Prime Minister Narendra Modi was aware. He challenged Modi to a public debate he said would expose foreign-controlled anti-national activities and end the PM's career, mocking him for needing a script. Congress shared the video on X. Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav backed Rahul, citing AI-era distrust of technology. BJP dismissed the claim; Kerala chief Rajeev Chandrasekhar called it absurd and attacked Gandhi personally. Amit Shah earlier urged a debate in Parliament instead of on the streets.}**visual**: {
items.title: Rahul Gandhi Accuses Modi Government of Tapping His Phone; BJP Rejects Debate Challenge

items.summary: India has invited Pakistan to the inaugural Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum, held November 20-22 at Purana Qila in New Delhi. Culture minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat expressed hope that Islamabad would attend despite strained bilateral ties. India sent invitations to 25 countries; 15 have confirmed participation so far, including China, Iran and Kazakhstan. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will open the event.
items.title: India Invites Pakistan to Inaugural SCO Civilisational Forum in Delhi

items.summary: Nvidia's board is weighing dismissal of CEO Jensen Huang amid a scandal involving his affair with an alleged Chinese spy, compounded by reports of a second affair. The company reportedly hired an outside search firm to find a successor, with some board members favoring the current CFO as interim leader and adding a COO. Firing Huang would end his 33-year tenure at the AI-boom-era semiconductor giant.
items.title: Nvidia Weighs Firing CEO Following Spying Scandal

items.summary: Long before GPS, Tanmen fishermen navigated the South China Sea using knowledge passed down through generations. Veteran captain Lu Jiabing recalls how they found their way to Huangyan Dao (Scarborough Shoal): following the Genglubu current, consulting a compass and even reading clouds to locate distant reefs.
items.title: Finding the Way to Huangyan Dao

items.summary: European leaders met in Dublin, hosted by Ireland's Micheál Martin, to seek a lead EU negotiator as peace talks with Russia expand. António Costa and Kaja Kallas were named as likely candidates, while von der Leyen insisted Europe must be included to safeguard interests.
items.title: EU Leaders Meet in Dublin Amid Search for Lead Negotiator on Ukraine Peace Talks

items.summary: Getting a heating system right hinges on an accurate heat loss calculation, measured in watts and worked out room by room to size the equipment. Cool Calc, used daily by roughly 150 new users including private homeowners, illustrates growing DIY interest. Yet studies suggest tradespeople often overestimate design loads by two or more times, risking oversized systems that waste power and cause uncomfortable temperature swings. Surveys can even cost up to $2,500 (£745). Experts disagree on the fix: some firms promote homeowner self-surveys via apps like Heatpunk and Dwellow's estimator, while others stress better installer practice rather than expecting owners to do engineering themselves.
items.title: Heat pumps: How much heat does your home really need?

items.summary: In response to a letter on active ageing amid longer working lives, Sport Singapore (SportSG) says it will review programme timing and availability. Active Health Labs extended hours since January with evening/weekend offerings like the Balance and Muscular Fitness Workshop and eight-week Strength 1.0. Citizens aged 65+ get free gym/pool access; senior-friendly machines are at 19 gyms, and credits offset fees.
items.title: SportSG Reviews Sports Programmes for Working Seniors

items.summary: Geopolitical shocks have reframed domestic clean energy as a strategic necessity, though temporary fossil fuel declines from supply disruptions won't yield lasting emissions cuts. The latest Global Carbon Budget projects 2026 fossil CO₂ down only 0.4% to 38.2 billion tonnes, while total CO₂ rises to 43.3 billion tonnes—underscoring that replacing fuels matters more than using less. India imports roughly 88% of crude oil and still draws over 93% of primary energy from fossil sources; renewables now supply about a quarter of electricity but curtailment wastes clean power, leaving coal to fill gaps after dark. Its ethanol programme saved foreign exchange yet strained maize supplies. Developing nations face high borrowing costs and limited finance at COP31 in Türkiye.
items.title: Geopolitical Shocks Put Energy Security and Clean Transition in Focus

items.summary: The Confederation of African Football is seeking hosts for the 2028, 2031 and 2033 Africa Cup of Nations editions after reversing its December decision to hold the tournament every four years instead of biennially. CAF has invited bids from all 54 member associations, with a declaration deadline next Tuesday and full documentation due by December 8. The 2027 edition is co-hosted by Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda.
items.title: CAF Seeks Hosts for Three Future Africa Cup of Nations Finals

items.summary: Heavy autumn rains are worsening conditions for civilians in Gaza, with torrential rainfall over the weekend killing at least six people. Local authorities report that at least 70,000 tents were flooded and more than 200,000 people affected. Residents describe difficult living conditions as they struggle to keep their homes dry and warm. The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) reported aid efforts benefiting an estimated 30,000 families through clearing blocked sewer lines at 60 locations. However, OCHA warned there is insufficient space to relocate people from flooded areas or war-damaged buildings due to Israeli restrictions on movement behind the Yellow Line. Save the Children's regional director Ahmad Alhendawi stated that around 1. 2 million people, including more than 560,000 children, live in critical or catastrophic shelter conditions, with available supplies covering less than 1% of needs for winter clothing and heating.
items.title: Humanitarian Crisis in Gaza Amid Political Deadlock and Approaching Winter

items.summary: As diplomatic efforts seek an end to Russia's war on Ukraine, a negotiated settlement remains unlikely due to Moscow's irreconcilable territorial demands, competing European security visions, and an increasingly unpredictable pro-Moscow US. Analyst Mark Galeotti of Mayak Intelligence argues that Putin's maximalist vision conceals a more complex negotiating strategy. The dispute over Donbas is especially obstructive: Russia seeks control of the entire region while Ukraine refuses to cede territory it still holds.
items.title: Putin Seeks to 'Hammer' Ukraine Amid Unlikely Negotiation Prospects

items.summary: Recent cyberattacks increasingly target physical infrastructure, not just data. In the past two weeks alone, hackers raised supermarket refrigerator temperatures across 12 countries spoiling tons of food, launched a $6.3 billion cryptocurrency heist from Binance attributed to North Korea's Lazarus group, and attacked water facilities in 12 U.S. states. Experts like Mikko Hyppönen warn that AI has accelerated vulnerability discovery far faster than patching—now occurring before flaws are disclosed—and lowered attack costs, enabling full automation. The digital-physical barrier is eroding: spoiled food cannot be recovered from a backup. Motives span profit, espionage and chaos, reflecting growing systemic fragility.
items.title: Cyberattacks Already Disrupt Everyday Infrastructure as AI Accelerates Threats

items.summary: The Invest in Tomorrow Coalition (ITC) super PAC, funded and led by solar entrepreneurs, targeted politicians who undermined clean-energy policy with attack ads. It won all six primaries it ran in 2025, then engaged 17 general-election races—winning desired outcomes in 13—and spent $17 million overall for a projected 83% success rate (19 of 23). Its targets included House Freedom Caucus members; 40% of those who signed a May 2025 letter to repeal the Inflation Reduction Act will not return. ITC deliberately targeted underfunded Democratic challengers, often obscuring its policy aim behind ads on other topics. The group credits its impact on establishing credible electoral consequences for clean-energy votes.
items.title: Invest in Tomorrow Coalition PAC's Congressional Retribution Against Clean-Energy Opponents

items.summary: Global fossil fuel emissions are expected to dip this year for the first time since 2020, driven by war rather than plague. The Iran war has caused brutal increases in oil and natural gas prices, leading many countries to cut their consumption of these fuels and seek alternatives. Fossil-fuel-related emissions will tick down by less than half a percent this year compared to 2025 per new data from the Global Carbon Project.
items.title: The Iran War Will Cause Global Fossil Fuel Emissions to Fall

items.summary: This illustrated feature showcases English properties sold near cosy pubs, ranging from a Cornish cottage linked to the TV series Doc Martin to a duplex above a historic pub in central London. The collection highlights homes positioned close to traditional public houses across varied locations.
items.title: Homes for Sale Near Cosy Pubs in England – In Pictures

items.summary: CNOOC Tianjin drilled a high-yield gas well to 5,770 meters in the central Bohai Sea volcanic rock, testing ~800,000 cubic meters of daily gas. With reservoir temperatures at 150 degrees Celsius and formation pressure above 80 megapascals, Guo Tao noted its significance for offshore ultra-deep exploration.
items.title: China Drills High-Yield Gas Well in Bohai Sea Volcanic Rock

items.summary: On a rainy Saturday in Decatur, Georgia, volunteers gathered at a repair café to fix broken furniture and electronics for free—Lilly Pettus among them, repairing a family dining chair she had owned for decades. These gatherings are one of several hundred across the United States, where Americans increasingly resist throwaway consumerism amid rising inflation. Repair Café International reports that in 2025 cafés prevented nearly 2 million pounds of waste and cut greenhouse gas emissions equivalent to about 1,000 Dutch families' consumption. While broken products are harder to repair due to corporate practices detailed in the FTC's report “Nixing the Fix,” right-to-repair laws now exist in four U.S. states and the European Union. Postma hopes for broader change, including a raw-materials tax. Cafés vary by neighborhood: at Collier Heights, Atlanta—where median household income is roughly $40,000 lower than Decatur's—attendees like Gale Pines fix items out of necessity rather than sentiment.
items.title: The Cozy Radicalism of Repair Cafés

items.summary: Shenzhen's Grepow launched a sodium-ion pouch-cell series on Nov. 12, adding the chemistry alongside its nickel-metal hydride and lithium polymer lines to target industrial equipment needing short high-current bursts in cold weather.
items.title: Grepow Launches Cold-Climate Sodium-Ion Pouch Cells for Industrial Niche

items.summary: Between 2020 and 2024, more than nine lakh Indians gained citizenship in the 38-member Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development. Numbers rose from 6.5 lakh to 9.2 lakh (a 41% jump), with Canada leading at 2.6 lakh (+150%). The Ministry of External Affairs reported nearly nine lakh Indian citizens relinquished their citizenship in the same period, declining annually from 85,256 in 2020 to 2 lakh in 2024. Overall OECD migration fell 19% for India in 2024, driven by a halving of UK flows to 66,000 persons.
items.title: Indians Gaining OECD Citizenship and Migration Trends (2020-2024)

items.summary: A tribute band honoring José Pinhal, a little-known northern Portuguese singer who died at 41 in 1993, played its farewell concerts after ten years. The band began as a joke in 2016 but grew into a viral phenomenon once his songs were uploaded to YouTube; one track now has around 1.4 million views and was used by an online betting company. Marina Pinhal, the singer's daughter, commented on the video that year, helping reveal who he was. The band—founded largely by João Sarnadas and featuring Bruno de Seda (Bruno Martins) as vocalist—delivered final shows at the Coliseums of Porto and Lisbon. Although critics note his music borrowed from Brazilian and Spanish artists rather than being original, fans praise its authenticity.
items.title: José Pinhal's Rediscovered Songs Sell Out Porto and Lisbon Coliseums

items.summary: Congress leader Shashi Tharoor alleged that 115 speakers scheduled for the two-day Bharat Summit in Hyderabad were denied entry or had visas cancelled, apparently on Ministry of Home Affairs instructions. The Congress-led Telangana government organized the summit, with organizers citing about 200 international delegates attending and political clearance obtained for foreign participants.
items.title: Congress Leader Alleges Denial of Entry for Bharat Summit Speakers Amid Journalist Visa Cancellations

items.summary: Nvidia lost founding CEO Jensen Huang, who resigned on Nov 12 amid disclosures of relationships with a woman identified as a Chinese spy and an executive reporting to him. Shares fell 14% in five days, though analysts expect little near-term business impact given Nvidia's dominant AI chip position—holding about 90% of the advanced AI chip market—with cash reserves enabling continued investment. The article draws on Silicon Valley succession history: Steve Jobs' return at Apple after John Sculley; Tim Cook and later John Ternus leading Microsoft (valued at US$5.16 trillion, S$6.65 trillion); Andrew Grove's Intel tenure followed by Craig Barrett as fortunes declined; Bill Gates handing CEO to sales-focused Steve Ballmer before Satya Nadella refocused the company toward cloud computing (Microsoft valued at US$3.88 trillion). Experts advise Nvidia's board to choose a technically grounded successor, noting Huang had not fully mapped out Nvidia's future despite his decades of success.
items.title: Nvidia's Leadership Succession After Jensen Huang Resignation

items.summary: The ggml-org team released llama.cpp libraries at version 1.0.0, marking a milestone after 3.5 years of growth (s3). The project runs multi-modal LLMs across hardware from consumer machines to enterprise servers via quantization and portable C/C++ backends (s0-s1). With support for more than 150 architecture variants (s22), the team prioritizes a stable API, stricter versioning boundaries, improved CI infrastructure backed by Hugging Face technologies and contributions from NVIDIA, AMD, Qualcomm, Arm, IBM and Intel (s7-s16).
items.title: llama.cpp v1.0.0 : A stronger foundation for the local AI ecosystem

items.summary: When former Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang resigned amid espionage allegations, Singapore-based retail investors rushed to buy the chipmaker's shares. Asiya Bakht, a 52-year-old PR founder, snapped up more stock as prices fell, with her holding now worth five figures. Trading surged across brokers: Syfe saw orders hit about 13 times their daily average, while FSM Global recorded volume at roughly 11 times its October level and IG nearly six times the prior week's. Nvidia shares dropped another 14% on Nov 12, adding to an 11% weekly decline that wiped about US$490 billion (S$630 billion) off market value. Some investors hedged with options; others like banker Joel Tan sold holdings amid leadership uncertainty.
items.title: Singapore Retail Investors Buy Nvidia Dip After Jensen Huang Scandal and Resignation

items.summary: On Friday, South Korea's Science and ICT Minister Bae Kyung-hoon confirmed that Nvidia will proceed with its pledge to supply 260,000 advanced GPUs. The commitment was reached last year at APEC meetings when Jensen Huang visited the country. It stands despite his resignation as chief executive. Both sides will continue joint projects including linking Korean-made AI chips with Nvidia's platform and building AI infrastructure.
items.title: South Korea Says Nvidia Will Keep GPU Pledges After Huang's Resignation

items.summary: On Friday (Nov 13), China warned the United States against adding export controls on semiconductors amid the Nvidia scandal. Foreign ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning said Beijing opposes abusing such measures, which disrupt global supply chains and serve no one's interests, urging continued cooperation under existing US-China consensus. The controversy stems from co-founder Jensen Huang's resignation over an affair with Alice Huang of Singapore-based Megaspeed, a company reportedly suspected by the Commerce Department—under Secretary Howard Lutnick—of rerouting restricted Nvidia technology to China.
items.title: China Warns Against New US Chip Export Controls After Nvidia Scandal

items.summary: Bloomberg reported that Aperia Cloud Services, an official Nvidia partner in Singapore, purchased servers containing banned H800 chips from Dell Technologies; those servers later reached Shanghai Longteng Intelligent Computing. The U.S. had barred H800 exports to China in 2023 amid concerns about circumvention of restrictions aimed at slowing Beijing's AI development.
items.title: Chinese Firm Linked to Alice Huang Acquired Banned Nvidia Chips

items.summary: Filings list servers worth 485 million yuan ($73 million) as collateral, including units with restricted Nvidia chips. Megaspeed, which Alice Huang founded in 2023, is under investigation for allegedly illegally shipping Nvidia chips into China and has denied the allegations. The hardware included 52 Super Micro Computer servers fitted with H100 or H200 processors from Nvidia.
items.title: Documents Tie Banned Nvidia AI Chips to Alice Huang-Linked Shanghai Data Center

items.summary: A major global Microsoft outage has disrupted or disabled services including email and AI products, with no cyber-security incident involved; instead Microsoft attributed it to elevated load after many servers became unexpectedly unavailable. Over 430 million people use Microsoft 365 apps, though Downdetector recorded only 140,000 reports from 74 countries on Thursday evening, likely undercounting the true scale. Disruption has spread worldwide: OpenAI and Anthropic reported problems, courts in Los Angeles to Texas warned of delays, Toronto hospitals faced email issues without affecting patient care, Japan's shared IT platform was disrupted, and UK GP surgeries, pharmacies, police and schools were impacted. The outage lasted more than 20 hours; experts say the failure snowballs as devices keep trying to reconnect during recovery.
items.title: What we know about the global Microsoft outage

items.summary: The International Energy Agency reports the world's oil supply has swung back into surplus for the first time since the start of the US-Israeli war against Iran, with October supplies outstripping demand by nearly 2m barrels a day as Gulf exports recovered faster than global demand. After months of Hormuz-blocked shipments and Brent crude spiking from $72 to $126 before falling toward $95, the IEA now forecasts supply averaging 105m barrels daily in Q4—1.7m above forecast demand—and expects members to release emergency stockpiles adding another 71m barrels by late February.
items.title: IEA Reports Global Oil Supply Returns to Surplus After Iran War Disruptions

items.summary: At least 74 countries have been affected by a Microsoft 365 outage, which disrupted Teams, Outlook and Copilot since it was detected after midday US Eastern Time on Thursday. The company reported encouraging recovery in Europe while North America also improved. In the US, House staff halted work; OpenAI investigated connection issues; courts warned of delays; Workhorse Group rescheduled its earnings report to 16 November from 12 November. Canadian hospitals, Via Rail and municipalities urged phone contact instead of email. In Japan some firms switched to fax machines while government IT was disrupted. Singapore's courts faced email problems but kept emergency services running. India's equity traders panicked over lost research reports; China users relied on Outlook for international communication despite the Great Firewall. Australia's spy agencies reported minimal impact, mostly affecting email systems.
items.title: How the Microsoft outage has been felt around the world

items.summary: A Microsoft outage lasting nearly 18 hours disrupted Outlook, Teams and Copilot worldwide from Thursday to Friday, drawing about 200,000 user reports. The failure affected AI firms OpenAI and Anthropic through their Microsoft 365 connectors, aviation via SpiceJet flight cancellations in India, and IT services broadly. Experts note that even a few hours of disruption can ripple into reduced output across the day, with severity varying by project. Unlike prior outages lasting only a few hours, this event underscored how organizations rely on single digital ecosystems for core operations like approvals and communication.
items.title: Microsoft Outage Exposes Dependence on Single Digital Ecosystem

items.summary: Nvidia's chief executive Jensen Huang had unusually close access to President Donald Trump, having joined him on trips and been briefed directly. His reported affair with Alice Huang—a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed—has raised suspicions that Chinese intelligence was targeting someone near the president. US officials suspect links between Huang and Beijing; China denies them. The controversy centers on Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who reportedly resisted acting against Megaspeed despite a classified memo warning of risks, while Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent pushed for action. Nvidia intervened in an investigation into suspected chip smuggling. Members of Congress from both parties are demanding answers as pressure mounts.
items.title: How a sex scandal at Nvidia is putting pressure on the White House

items.summary: A worldwide outage of critical Microsoft systems disrupted businesses and public services, affecting millions for over 12 hours before the company reported early signs of stabilisation. More than 430 million people use Microsoft 365 apps, with more than 90% of Fortune 500 companies relying on its Copilot AI chatbot; no cyber-attack was indicated as a cause.
items.title: Global Microsoft Outage and Other Top Stories

items.summary: Nvidia announced that CEO Jensen Huang is stepping down after admitting to extramarital affairs, including one with a client allegedly recruited by China's top spy agency. CFO Colette Kress becomes interim CEO during the AI-chip crisis. The scandal raises questions at the White House and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick about chip export restrictions. Separately, Sen. Chris Van Hollen will challenge Chuck Schumer for Senate majority leader, citing voter desire for change.
items.title: Nvidia CEO steps down. And, Sen. Chris Van Hollen to run for majority leader

items.summary: In a Politics Weekly America podcast, Jonathan Freedland speaks with New Yorker's Susan Glasser about why Donald Trump's judgment of high-profile men appears questionable. The discussion centers on how the Nvidia cheating scandal complicates Trump's handling of prominent figures and his own credibility.
items.title: Why the Nvidia cheating scandal is bad for Trump

items.summary: On Tata Motors' Q2 FY27 earnings call, MD-CEO Shailesh Chandra said absolute volumes would stay strong but cost pressures persisted into the third quarter. Passenger Vehicles posted a Rs 5,531 crore loss versus Rs 76,170 crore profit last year, though consolidated revenue rose to Rs 96,920 crore from Rs 72,349 crore. The company offset about 40% of commodity cost impact and expects Q4 relief via price hikes and cost cuts.
items.title: Tata Motors Q3 Cost Pressure and JLR China Uncertainty

items.summary: Nvidia's stock fell more than 13% at Thursday's open after reports that its board was preparing to remove co-founder Jensen Huang, whose 33-year tenure ended in resignation. The departure followed an independent investigation into spying allegations tied to foreign intelligence efforts, alongside revelations of personal misconduct and a reported relationship with colleague Kimberly Powell. Huang held only about 3.6% of Nvidia through family trusts and direct holdings, without super-voting shares, so the board retained decision-making authority. Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO while searching for a permanent replacement.
items.title: Jensen Huang Exits Nvidia as CEO Amid Spying Allegations and Leadership Uncertainty

items.summary: Following Jensen Huang's resignation amid a personal scandal, Nvidia lost about $1.8tn (€1.6tn) in market value since its October 6 record close of $239.24 per share. Colette Kress now leads as interim CEO while the board seeks a permanent successor. Analysts debate whether investors will accept continued dealmaking pace and how much growth remains if customers slow AI spending. Price targets have fallen sharply, with Yorkville Ives at $225 (down 25% from $300), Bernstein and Baird at $200, Citi at $225, and Goldman Sachs holding a buy rating at $220.
items.title: Nvidia’s $1.8tn Value Drop After Jensen Huang Departure

items.summary: 2026 began with Wall Street's trillion-dollar AI bet paying off, but a second-half sell-off—triggered by midterm results and Nvidia turmoil over alleged ties to a suspected Chinese spy—erased more than $1 trillion from the Magnificent Seven in one day. Analysts dispute whether this signals a bursting bubble or merely a healthy correction amid roughly $800 billion of 2026 capex, with further spending planned through 2028.
items.title: Is the AI Bubble Bursting as Anthropic Goes Public?

items.summary: This article explores the environmental and economic costs of dependence on a few large technology companies, using cloud computing as its central example. It notes that data centres consumed 415 terawatt-hours in 2024 (about 1.5% of global demand), projected to reach 945 terawatt-hours by 2030 largely due to AI. Microsoft reported a 25% rise in total emissions in 2025, driven by expanding data centres and accounting changes. The piece links software lock-in—exemplified by Windows 10 support ending in October 2025—to reduced consumer choice over greener alternatives, and cites global e-waste of 62 million metric tonnes (only 22.3% formally recycled) plus US$78 billion (£59 billion) in externalised costs in 2022. It calls for procurement decisions based on lifetime cost, lifespan and emissions rather than the next annual bill.
items.title: The Costs of Digital Dependence on Microsoft and Cloud Technology

items.summary: A global Microsoft outage since Thursday afternoon has disrupted Outlook, Teams, Copilot and other services across Portugal. The Ministry of Health's Shared Services confirmed affected bodies are working to restore access, while government ministers reportedly lost email but continued using an unaffected internal network plus WhatsApp and Signal. Schools face communication breakdowns between parents, teachers and pupils. Microsoft attributes the issue to a configuration update causing server overload, rules out cyberattack, and offers no restoration timeframe.
items.title: Global Microsoft Outage Disrupts Portugal Government, Schools and Health Services

items.summary: The global Microsoft 365 outage on Nov 13 disrupted Outlook, Teams and Copilot for more than half a day, spilling into Asia-Pacific business hours. Singapore saw government systems and several banks' email affected, while emergency services and Singpass stayed operational. Experts frame this as an 'over-reliance' problem: efficiency gains from consolidating with major cloud vendors create single points of failure that can cascade across industries. NTU's Boh Wai Fong calls it a 'paradox of digital transformation.' Anupam Chattopadhyay warns the massive complexity makes failures hard to isolate and repair, risking cascading effects. Liu Yang stresses redundancy does not guarantee resilience when services share infrastructure. Choo notes impacts extend beyond email into core business processes, with AI amplifying future risks.
items.title: What the Microsoft Outlook outage reveals about risks, limitations and gaps in communication

items.summary: The removal of Jensen Huang as CEO of Nvidia, the company he led for 33 years, has sent shockwaves through global tech. Nvidia supplies 90% of chips used in data centre servers where sophisticated AI models are trained. The scandal emerged amid a race between major powers to gain supremacy in transformative technology. Allegations that Huang had an affair with a businesswoman reportedly linked to the Chinese government raised national security concerns, prompting bipartisan demands for explanations from Trump and Huang. Lawmakers including Senator John Thune and Representatives Brian Mast and John Moolenaar pushed for testimony or subpoenas. Senators Elizabeth Warren and others insist his resignation does not absolve him of responsibility.
items.title: Congress Demands Answers Over Nvidia Espionage Allegations and Jensen Huang Scandal

items.summary: The fallout from allegations that Nvidia chief Jensen Huang was entangled with Alice Huang, suspected of Chinese intelligence links, has reframed a corporate scandal as a national-security concern. Former CIA and FBI officials warn honey traps—using intimacy to compromise targets—are an enduring vulnerability harder than firewalls or passwords to defend against. The affair exposes China's layered machinery: the Ministry of State Security, once cautious with its "thousand grains of sand" approach but more aggressive after 2005; military intelligence units including a former PLA department estimated at over 100,000 personnel; and cyber operations tracing to lessons from the Gulf War. Investigations by Congress, the FBI and Nvidia's board remain unfinished, with no public proof Alice Huang was an operative. The case underscores that foreign services increasingly target AI, quantum computing and biotechnology—and that breaches may begin not with sophisticated hacking but ordinary human connections.
items.title: Nvidia Scandal as a Window Into China's Broader Espionage Machine

items.summary: For India's emerging neocloud providers—Yotta, E2E Networks and Neysa—access to computing power is the business. These specialized cloud operators let enterprises, startups and research institutions rent high-performance GPUs rather than invest in their own infrastructure, positioning them as an important layer in India's AI ecosystem. Yet this boom rests on heavy dependence on a single company: NVIDIA—which now faces leadership turmoil and supply-chain risks.
items.title: India's AI infrastructure bet hinges on NVIDIA amid leadership crisis and supply-chain risks

items.summary: Nvidia lacked a succession plan for ousted founder-CEO Jensen Huang, though it had attempted to hire an external number two before his departure. Candidates avoided working in his shadow; one Slack group titled 'Stand with Jensen' exists, and few fewer than 10 people worldwide are seen as capable of running the company. The successor must keep Nvidia's products shipping on time while sustaining the entire industry—no replacement is readily available.
items.title: Nvidia's Next CEO Must Keep an Entire Industry Alive

items.summary: CoreWeave, whose stock has been volatile on the Nvidia saga, is pursuing a $4 billion loan syndicated by Morgan Stanley and Mitsubishi UFJ. The debt will be collateralized by contracts with Meta, allowing CoreWeave to benefit from Meta's strong credit standing. Early marketing reception was positive, with an all-in interest rate around 7.5%, far cheaper than the nearly 16% yield its unsecured bonds have hit.
items.title: CoreWeave Secures $4B Loan Backed by Meta Contracts Amid Nvidia Uncertainty

items.summary: Reuters obtained an internal Amazon document describing 'World Product Graph,' a plan to aggregate product information on virtually every item sold worldwide, whether or not Amazon stocks it. The initiative aims to make Amazon the definitive shopping destination, reduce reliance on Google for research, fend off Walmart's e-commerce growth, and counter AI shopping agents like Meta's Muse (over 10 million users) that direct traffic elsewhere. A related search agent, Rufus ('Alexa for Shopping'), reportedly gives inaccurate answers despite claims of ~97% accuracy globally; Amazon says usage figures are outdated. The project falls under VP Robert Tekiela and may involve brands such as Coca-Cola, Bayer, and Procter & Gamble contributing data or Amazon crawling retailer sites.
items.title: Exclusive-Amazon’s plan to own the world’s product data and fight AI shopping agents

items.summary: Singapore-based investor Leo Chengwon Kohan, who has invested roughly $1.3 billion in Nvidia and holds a net worth of about $13.2 billion per the Bloomberg Billionaires Index, refused to add further capital after former CEO Jensen Huang's removal over alleged affairs and espionage suspicions. Kohan demanded Huang's reinstatement as 'supreme creator' of AI and superintelligence chips, citing support from Elon Musk, Gavin Becker and President Trump; he plans reduced Nvidia investment while funding other superintelligence firms.
items.title: Nvidia Investor Leo Chengwon Kohan Halts Further Investment Over Jensen Huang Ouster

items.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent criticized Nvidia and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick for weak controls over chip exports, citing significant leakage in the system. The remarks followed reports that Jensen Huang had affairs with Alice Huang, a Chinese spy suspect, prompting his resignation as CEO. Colette Kress will serve as interim leader while the board searches for a permanent successor.
items.title: Bessent Criticizes Nvidia and Lutnick Over Chip Export Controls Amid Huang Scandal

items.summary: An evening news roundup covers a Microsoft 365 outage lasting over 16 hours, with gradual but incomplete service restoration. At least 23 people died when a mini-bus collided with a truck near Kaziranga in Assam. Rahul Gandhi accused the Modi government of phone surveillance; Nvidia fell up to 14%, dropping below $4 trillion market value; cash-strapped SpiceJet called an emergency board meeting.
items.title: Microsoft Outage Recovery; Kaziranga Crash Kills 23; Nvidia Slump and Other Business Stories

items.summary: A major global outage at Microsoft disrupted email and cloud-based services across the world on Thursday, affecting businesses, government agencies and public services in 74 countries and territories. The disruption began Thursday and continued into Friday, hitting Microsoft 365 — including Outlook, Teams, SharePoint, OneDrive and Copilot — with Exchange Online at its core. Downdetector received reports from users in 74 countries within about an hour, with Outlook problems peaking around 130,000 in the US. Microsoft said servers unexpectedly stopped working, then failed again under returning traffic, while reversing a recent network configuration change; executive vice president Charles Lamanna noted no sign of a cyberattack. Impacts were widespread: governments and courts resorted to paper or phone calls, banks confirmed transactions by fax, healthcare facilities reverted to paper prescriptions, airlines reported customer-support disruptions, and companies like Workhorse postponed events.
items.title: Global Microsoft Outage Disrupted Services Worldwide

items.summary: Computer scientist and podcaster Lex Fridman has publicly backed Jensen Huang after his exit from Nvidia, calling the departure a 'huge mistake for America and humanity' and likening it to Apple firing Steve Jobs in 1985. Huang resigned unconditionally late Wednesday amid reports of two extramarital affairs, including one with a woman suspected of spying for China. Colette Kress was appointed interim CEO, while director Harvey Jones, 73, became the board's first-ever chair. Fridman defended Huang as an extremely proud American and described him as kind, humble, and caring, noting that more than 1,000 close associates praised his character privately.
items.title: Podcaster Lex Fridman Defends Jensen Huang's Ouster From Nvidia

items.summary: Jensen Huang's resignation from Nvidia has drawn concern in Israel, the company's 'second home.' While Nvidia and other firms like Intel and Microsoft invest heavily there—Nvidia employs 6,000 locals—the leadership crisis may loosen its grip. Investors worry slower decisions could open room for challengers building AI-specific chips and inference software, though uncertainty might also shrink overall spending.
items.title: Israel's VCs See Opportunity for Challengers in Nvidia's Turmoil

items.summary: The Wall Street Journal reports that outgoing NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang called interim CFO Collette Kress "a deer in the headlights," saying she couldn't help steer strategy. She has 13 years at NVIDIA and questioned credit-based deals tied to son-in-law Nico Caprez, scaling back OpenAI's Ohio commitment from $250 billion to $105 billion. Huang resigned Thursday over two reported affairs; a third was later reported by Reuters.
items.title: Jensen Huang's lukewarm view of successor Kress

items.summary: On Friday, Microsoft reported completing recovery actions across parts of its affected Asia Pacific infrastructure as traffic gradually restored, though Microsoft 365 services including Outlook remained disrupted for a second day. Mailbox access improved while some users faced intermittent issues; the focus shifted to extending recovery elsewhere and reducing email backlogs.
items.title: Microsoft Asia Pacific Outage Recovery and Outlook Disruption Continue

items.summary: Megaspeed International is the company linked to Nvidia chief Jensen Huang's resignation over alleged extramarital affairs with an accused Chinese spy, Alice Huang. US agencies believe Huang acted as a Chinese intelligence asset passing commercial information to Beijing; China flatly rejects these claims. Megaspeed's global facades are puzzling: near-empty offices in Singapore and Kuala Lumpur, a dilapidated storefront in Malaysia, and no physical presence for its Australian subsidiary on the 10th floor of a Sydney building. Despite purchasing nearly $5bn in Nvidia chips over three years, representatives know nothing about it. Alice Huang was barred from re-entering Singapore and Taiwan; Kai Kang remains unaccounted for. Analysts warn Megaspeed could be a front for Chinese intelligence or simply make the parent look credible.
items.title: The baffling corporate trail of Megaspeed International amid Jensen Huang's downfall

items.summary: A 2024 photo of Akshay Kumar joking with NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang has resurfaced as meme material following Huang's resignation amid a personal scandal. Users recast the image sarcastically and in Bollywood film scenes, while attention shifted to Indian-origin board member Aarti Shah, who joined Nvidia's Audit and Compensation Committees in 2020 after nearly three decades at Eli Lilly.
items.title: Akshay Kumar's Nvidia Compliment Becomes Meme After Jensen Huang Resignation

items.summary: Oracle faces mounting pressure as it winds down a 2023 Microsoft deal to rent AI computing for its Copilot assistant, reportedly because the Nvidia chips powering it were already outdated. This mirrors an earlier $7 billion chip cancellation with Tencent under Trump administration pressure. The moves underscore investor anxieties about AI infrastructure becoming obsolete before recouping costs and mismatched build timelines.
items.title: Microsoft Winding Down Oracle AI Deal Signals Broader Concerns

items.summary: Microsoft warned that its November 2026 security updates can break printing of documents with complex formatting, specifically images rendered at zero height or width. The issue mainly affects Microsoft Word files printed via GDI on Windows Server and client devices running Windows 10 or later.
items.title: Microsoft's November 2026 Updates Break Printing for Complex Documents

items.summary: A major Microsoft outage attributed to elevated load on its infrastructure disrupted email, Teams and Copilot globally within an hour, affecting users in 74 countries and territories across the Americas, Europe, Asia and Africa. Microsoft confirmed repair efforts were not proceeding as expected and was pursuing alternate workstreams to increase capacity, without stating when full service would be restored.
items.title: Microsoft Outlook Outage Disrupts Users Across 74 Countries

items.summary: One 97 Communications said its subsidiary Paytm Payments Services Ltd received in-principle authorisation from the Reserve Bank of India on November 13, 2026 to operate prepaid payment instruments through a letter dated that day. The approval is subject to RBI Master Directions and requires system and cyber security audits by qualified auditors before PPSL can issue wallets; final issuance needs separate certificate authorisation. Paytm reported over 10-fold profit growth to Rs 225 crore, operating revenue up 28% YoY to Rs 2,648 crore, and record Ebitda of Rs 270 crore in Q2 ended September 2026.
items.title: Paytm's PPSL Gets RBI In-Principle Approval for Wallet Operations Amid Strong Q2 Growth

items.summary: Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles swung to a consolidated net loss of Rs 5,531 crore in the July–September quarter of FY27, down from a profit of Rs 76,170 crore a year earlier. A Rs 6,738 crore exceptional charge drove the loss and exceeded it by Rs 1,207 crore. Consolidated revenue rose 34 percent to Rs 96,920 crore as domestic momentum continued while JLR restructured.
items.title: Tata Motors PV Posts Q2 FY27 Loss Amid JLR Restructuring

items.summary: A field experiment in 43 Indian garment factories run by Shahi Exports tested whether an anonymous worker-voice tool, Inache (by Good Business Lab), raised productivity. Randomly assigned in 2019 into three groups—tool only, tool plus HR incentives, and control—the study found no significant effects for the tool alone, but meaningful gains where human-resources teams had measurable response targets tied to rewards. Absenteeism fell by -12.7% (about one percentage point against a 7.9% mean), monthly earnings rose +3.2%, and productivity increased +4.7% (against a 53% control mean). Turnover may have dropped (-6%), though that estimate is imprecise due to pandemic disruption. Gains came through faster, higher-quality HR responses and more grievances raised—830 total over the period—with production-related reports driving output gains by enabling fixes like fan repairs in heat.
items.title: Worker Voice Tools Raise Productivity Only With Aligned HR Incentives

items.summary: A global Microsoft outage disrupted Outlook, Teams and Copilot on Thursday, affecting millions of users across at least 74 countries with roughly 140,000 reports. Aviation was hit in India: IndiGo's email support is affected while Air India rerouted traffic but reported no flight disruption. Governments, financial markets and AI firms OpenAI and Anthropic also faced issues.
items.title: Microsoft Outage Disrupts Outlook, Teams Globally; Indian Airlines Affected

items.summary: U.S. lawmakers on Thursday demanded clarity about what President Donald Trump knew regarding Nvidia chief Jensen Huang’s extramarital affair with a woman suspected of spying for China, after the AI chipmaker announced his departure. Huang had advocated looser rules on U.S. chip sales to China amid intensifying scrutiny ahead of Trump’s visit.
items.title: Congress Presses Trump and Nvidia Over Jensen Huang’s Exit

items.summary: Dyania Health's Synapsis AI is a clinical reasoning engine that processes patient records within hospital firewalls, using NVIDIA-accelerated computing to surface traceable evidence for clinician review. At Cleveland Clinic, it supported a study of more than 7,800 aortic valve replacement patients between 2005 and 2021, building predictive models of valve deterioration at three-, five- and ten-year intervals.
items.title: AI-Powered Clinical Reasoning Accelerates Patient Care at Dyania Health and Cleveland Clinic

items.summary: Google Cloud released TPU Sync, an open-source Apache-2.0 C++ library that moves key-value (KV) caches and model weights across the memory hierarchy of its TPUs using asynchronous DMA. The tool targets inference bottlenecks in large mixture-of-experts models, reporting over 90% lower KV transfer latency on 235B to 480B parameter MoE models during internal July 2026 tests on TPU v7x (Ironwood). It supports PyTorch via TorchTPU and JAX natively. Google notes all figures are self-reported, early-stage, and not yet recommended for general use.
items.title: Google Releases TPU Sync for Open-Source KV Cache Transfer on TPUs

items.summary: A Microsoft Outlook email outage left millions of individuals, organizations and businesses without access on Thursday, including NPR's newsroom. Down for more than 12 hours, the service reported only marginal success early Friday, attributing it to elevated load rather than malicious activity. Teams and Copilot were also affected across more than 70 countries.
items.title: Microsoft scrambles to fix email outage

items.summary: A widespread Microsoft outage disrupted access to Outlook, Teams, Copilot and other Microsoft 365 services worldwide, including India. Nearly 1.3 lakh users reported problems accessing Outlook shortly after 1 pm Eastern Time on Friday (November 13). While reports later declined, users continued facing email and inbox issues. Microsoft attributed the outage to servers unexpectedly failing health checks before becoming unavailable, with recovery attempts not working as expected; no cyberattack was indicated.
items.title: Widespread Microsoft Outage Disrupts Outlook, Teams and Copilot Globally

items.summary: Google DeepMind released Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a closed-weights model built for everyday agent loops. It features a 1,048,576-token unified window across input, thinking and output, served via the API only with no self-hosting or quantized variants. Google reports it scores 51 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at high level—above Gemini 4 Argon's 50—and reaches 57% on Terminal-Bench 4.1 versus 18.2% for Gemini 3.8 Flash. Priced at $1.50/$7.50 per million tokens, it is positioned as a faster daily driver that pairs with Carbon in Antigravity.
items.title: Google Releases Gemini 4 Hydrogen for Coding and Agentic Work

items.summary: European Commission published its long-awaited Digital Fairness Act (DFA), which would replace the Unfair Commercial Practices Directive with a directly applicable Regulation and ban manipulative design. Itxaso Domínguez de Olazábal of European Digital Rights (EDRi) welcomes parts, including a blacklist of ten dark patterns and recognition that using a service can be a commercial decision under Article 17. Yet the law largely relies on opt-outs for addictive features; its impact assessment estimated €13.7 billion in prevented consumer detriment annually. The proposal also narrowed protections for particularly vulnerable consumers to serious misfortune, excluding temporary or situational vulnerabilities. EDRi argues this places burden of proof on regulators and users rather than companies that design systems. It urges the European Parliament and Council to add proportionate obligations requiring traders to assess foreseeable risks before deploying harmful practices.
items.title: The EU Promises Digital Fairness, But Still Wants Users To Do the Work

items.summary: A major global outage brought Microsoft's widely used tools—including email and cloud storage—to a standstill, with around 130,000 people reporting Outlook access issues by early Thursday afternoon US Eastern time. The company said it was aggressively pursuing pathways to reduce impact while restarting affected servers. Impacts extended well beyond missed emails: family violence workers could not access client databases, schools lost remote lessons, psychologists lost telehealth capacity, businesses stalled on orders, and some government service centres closed. OpenAI and Anthropic also reported problems with their Microsoft 365 connections. The likely cause was a fault in the automated health-check machinery that withdraws servers it deems unwell, leaving healthy ones overwhelmed—an inference rather than a confirmed root cause.
items.title: Microsoft has suffered a global outage. A tech expert explains what went wrong

items.summary: The Ministry of External Affairs reiterated New Delhi's firm diplomatic posture toward Pakistan during a bi-weekly briefing, with spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal stressing that political clearances follow national policy. This follows Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann seeking clearance to attend the 4th International World Punjabi Conference in Lahore (November 27-29), where he was invited as chief guest. Mann also called for reopening the suspended Kartarpur Corridor amid strained India-Pakistan relations.
items.title: MEA Reaffirms India's Stance as Punjab CM Seeks Clearance for Lahore Visit

items.summary: Commentator Wang Yichen argues that right-wing forces in Japan are repackaging militarist symbols as entertainment to normalize them among young people. Evidence includes a rising sun flag banned then reinstated at an Asian Games venue, its appearance at a World Cup match, and controversial depictions of war crimes in anime, manga, films, and military emblems. The author contends that culture is not apolitical; rather, symbols retain their history regardless of context, as seen with Nazi insignia in Europe. This cultural infiltration prepares the social ground for Japan's neo-militarism by shaping a generation unfamiliar with war crimes through softened textbooks and screens.
items.title: Cultural Infiltration Paving the Way for Japan's Neo-Militarism

items.summary: Miami-based NAED Energy Holding rates its PV-1 PECVD-V vertical in-line deposition platform at 96,000 wafers per hour, double the previous XL-class line. It targets a T2X perovskite/HJT tandem cell aiming for 30% efficiency and glass-glass modules from 600 W. NAED says six of 13 process tools are complete; figures are rated or target values.
items.title: NAED Energy Holding's Vertical Deposition Line for Tandem Solar Cells

items.summary: Government data released Friday showed India's total exports rose 29.9% to USD 89.99 billion in October, up from USD 69.27 billion a year earlier. Total imports climbed to USD 110.07 billion from USD 94.42 billion. The trade deficit narrowed to USD 20.09 billion from USD 25.15 billion in the same month last year, per PTI reporting for Hindustan Times.
items.title: India's October Exports Jumped Nearly 30% as Trade Deficit Narrowed

items.summary: The 2026 APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, held November 18-19 at the Shenzhen International Exchange Center in Guangdong Province, will run entirely on green electricity. China Southern Power Grid (CSG) said preparations are complete and it secured 89 million kilowatt-hours of green power to cover all event energy use. Supply comes from offshore wind farms in Yangjiang plus wind and solar bases in northwest China's deserts, Gobi areas and barren lands, transmitted over long-distance interprovincial networks.
